newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up on tight liquidity.

text.p: The Philippine peso gained on Wednesday to 26.283 against the dollar at the close from 26.290 after banks sold dollars to ease tight money market conditions, traders said.
The peso was also boosted by dollar inflows, they said.
"Since (local) interest rates are higher, those long in dollars had no other recourse but to take losses," said dealer from a medium-sized bank.
The average interest rate at the money market rose to 12.0 percent from 11.59375, which makes it more expensive to hold on to dollars.
The day's peso average was at 26.282 to the dollar from 26.293, with turnover swelling to $268 million from $111.20 million.

In the past two weeks, banks have been adding to dollar holdings in anticipation that the peso will depreciate because a planned one percentage-point reduction in reserve requirements in January could lead to lower domestic interest rates in the longer-term.
But rates rose on Wednesday due to the money market tightness, dealers said.
The Central Bank bought some $113 million from 26.279 to 26.283 to limit the peso's strength, traders said.
The peso could weaken on Thursday as banks have sold enough dollars to ease their liquidity positions, a dealer predicted.
